documents.source_category: Interim Financial Statements for the Quarter ended 30th June 2026

financials_interim.notes: First Capital Treasuries PLC (FCT), a primary dealer in Government Securities and a subsidiary of First Capital Limited (itself a subsidiary of First Capital Holdings PLC, cluster parent). Single-entity Company only -- no subsidiaries, no Group/Company split anywhere in this filing (the cover page and every statement say 'FIRST CAPITAL TREASURIES PLC' only) -- GROUP basis used per this project's single-entity-filer convention (one row only). FYE 31 March (confirmed by the debenture note's 'year ended 31 March 2026' reference and the SOFP's 31.03.2026 comparative column). Q1 FY2026/27 (three months ended 30 June 2026, column 'April-June 2026' on the face P&L) vs Q1 FY2025/26 comparative (three months ended 30 June 2025, column 'April-June 2025') -- both explicitly presented side-by-side on the face Statement of Profit or Loss (printed page 2) and the face Statement of Cash Flows (printed page 5), a genuine same-quarter YoY compare. FIELD-MAPPING RATIONALE (bank/NBFI-style convention applied, per this project's guidance for primary dealer / treasury entities): FCT's P&L has NO conventional 'Revenue' line -- its income statement is built from 'Direct income' (906,391) less 'Direct expenses' (1,203,786) = 'Net trading income/(loss)' (-297,395), the equivalent of a bank's Net Interest Income (funding-cost-netted). revenue field = 'Net income/(loss) before operating expenses' (-909,354; 2025: 2,538,268), i.e. Net trading income (-297,395) + Other income (558,605, mostly a one-off Rs.552.1mn recovery of management fee/branch commission per Note 1.1) + Gain/(loss) on fair valuation of financial assets through P&L (-1,170,564) -- this is FCT's own 'Total Operating Income' equivalent, the true top-line after funding cost but before admin/S&D/other operating expenses, analogous to how bank entries in this database (e.g. NTB) map revenue = Total Operating Income. operating_profit field = 'Profit/(loss) before tax' (-1,054,037; 2025: 2,253,095) -- there is no intermediate operating-profit subtotal distinct from PBT in this filing (Net income before opex minus Operating expenses of -144,683 flows straight to PBT, with no separate finance cost/VAT-SSCL line below it), so operating_profit and profit_before_tax are numerically identical here; this is a genuine feature of the filing's structure, not a data-entry duplication. finance_costs/finance_income left BLANK -- funding cost is already netted into 'Direct expenses' within the revenue-equivalent line (same convention as the NTB bank entry, where interest expense is already netted into Net Interest Income). tax_expense = +312,841 (a NET TAX REVERSAL, not an expense -- 2026 was a loss-making quarter and the filing's own Note 2 shows a deferred tax asset of 312,841 recognised, with zero current tax; stored as a positive value per this database's sign convention where tax_expense adds directly to PBT to give PAT: -1,054,037 + 312,841 = -741,196, ties exactly to the filing's 'Profit/(loss) for the period'). Prior-year tax_expense = -699,708 (a genuine expense: current tax -617,433 + deferred tax reversal -82,275 per Note 2). eps_basic = eps_diluted = -1.20 (only one EPS line disclosed, no separate diluted figure; cross-check: -741,196k / 615,600k shares = -1.204, rounds to -1.20, ties). shares_in_issue = 615,600,000 per Note 6. BALANCE SHEET: FCT's Statement of Financial Position is UNCLASSIFIED (no current/non-current split presented anywhere for assets or liabilities, consistent with a bank/NBFI-style presentation) -- current_assets, current_liabilities, inventory, trade_receivables and trade_payables are all left BLANK per this project's bank/NBFI convention, not a data gap. total_assets = 62,310,126; total_liabilities = 55,401,965; total_equity = 6,908,161; identity check ties exactly (55,401,965 + 6,908,161 = 62,310,126). cash_and_equivalents = 'Cash at banks and in hand' = 61,297. BORROWINGS -- read carefully per this project's guidance that repo funding might BE the core business: short_term_borrowings = 'Securities sold under re-purchase agreements' = 51,855,213 -- this is FCT's dominant liability (93.6% of total liabilities) and is genuinely interest-bearing debt used to fund the Government Securities trading book (the Company's core business IS running a leveraged repo book), rolled short-term, so it is included as short_term_borrowings rather than excluded as a non-debt operating item (unlike, e.g., trade payables at a general company) -- this is a deliberate inclusion, documented here rather than left as an unexplained judgement call. long_term_borrowings = 'Borrowings on listed debentures' = 3,042,184 (30,000,000 x Rs.100 face value, 5-year subordinated Tier II debentures maturing 24 April 2030, per Note 5 and the Investor Information debenture table) -- genuinely long-dated debt, correctly separated from the repo book. CASH FLOW: unlike some other filings this batch, FCT's cash flow statement IS presented on a clean 3-month 'April-June' quarterly basis (not 6-month cumulative), matching the P&L period exactly -- no YTD/quarterly ambiguity here. cash_from_operations = 66,560 (Net cash from/(used in) operating activities); capex = -(240 + 40,740) = -40,980 (Purchase of PP&E 240 + Purchase of intangible assets 40,740; there were no disposal proceeds this quarter) -- ties exactly to cash_from_investing (-40,980) since those two lines are the entirety of the investing section this quarter. cash_from_financing = 0 (no debenture/other financing movement this quarter; prior-year comparative had a one-off Rs.3,000,000k debenture issuance). MARGIN CAVEAT (documented per this project's instruction to flag anything inconsistent): because revenue (-909,354) and operating_profit/PBT (-1,054,037) are BOTH NEGATIVE this quarter, the derived operating_margin and net_margin ratios in the interim_updates yoy_json are mathematically well-defined but NOT intuitively meaningful (dividing a larger loss by a smaller loss produces a ratio above 100%) -- these are flagged as directional-only in the narrative, not read as genuine profitability-margin trends. The quarter's loss is explicitly attributed by management's own Review of Operations (printed page 1) to (a) a 100bp CBSL policy rate hike in May 2026 and (b) adverse mark-to-market movements on the trading portfolio amid Middle East geopolitical tensions -- consistent with the Rs.1,170,564k fair-valuation loss being the single largest negative P&L driver, larger in magnitude than the entire net trading loss and other income combined.

interim_updates.note_text: First Capital Treasuries PLC (FCT) swung from a Profit After Tax of Rs.1,553.4mn in Q1 FY2025/26 (quarter ended 30 June 2025) to a Loss After Tax of Rs.741.2mn in Q1 FY2026/27 (quarter ended 30 June 2026), a swing of Rs.2,294.6mn, driven by adverse mark-to-market movements on its Government Securities trading book against a backdrop of a 100 basis point Central Bank of Sri Lanka policy rate hike in May 2026 and heightened market volatility linked to Middle East geopolitical tensions (per management's own Review of Operations). The single largest negative driver was a Rs.1,170.6mn loss on fair valuation of financial assets through profit or loss (2025: a Rs.744.6mn gain), a swing of Rs.1,915.2mn that alone exceeds the entire Rs.2,294.6mn PAT decline. Net trading income (Direct income of Rs.906.4mn less Direct expenses of Rs.1,203.8mn) was itself a loss of Rs.297.4mn, versus a Rs.1,787.3mn profit a year earlier, as Direct income fell 74.2% YoY (Rs.906.4mn vs Rs.3,513.0mn) while Direct expenses fell only 30.2% (Rs.1,203.8mn vs Rs.1,725.8mn) -- funding costs did not scale down with trading income. Partially offsetting this, Other Income rose to Rs.558.6mn (2025: Rs.6.4mn) almost entirely due to a one-off Rs.552.1mn recovery of management fee (Rs.216.8mn) and branch commission (Rs.238.6mn), plus Rs.96.7mn of interest thereon, previously charged by parent companies First Capital Holdings PLC and First Capital Limited under Central Bank of Sri Lanka guidelines -- a genuine one-off recovery, not a recurring income item. Operating expenses fell 49.3% YoY to Rs.144.7mn (2025: Rs.285.2mn), mainly on lower administrative expenses (Rs.133.2mn vs Rs.192.4mn, -30.8%) and a sharp drop in other operating expenses (Rs.7.6mn vs Rs.87.5mn, -91.3%), a genuine cost saving but far too small to offset the trading-book swing. The Company's own tax line moved from a Rs.699.7mn expense to a Rs.312.8mn net reversal (a Rs.312.8mn deferred tax asset recognised against the quarter's loss, with zero current tax payable), partially cushioning the pre-tax loss of Rs.1,054.0mn down to the Rs.741.2mn after-tax loss. On the balance sheet, the Government Securities trading book grew to Rs.60.35bn at 30 June 2026 from Rs.53.60bn at the start of the financial year (per management's Review of Operations), funded predominantly by an increase in repo borrowings (Securities sold under re-purchase agreements rose to Rs.51,855.2mn from Rs.43,213.1mn at 31 March 2026, +20.0% in the quarter) -- total net assets fell to Rs.6,908.2mn from Rs.7,649.4mn at the start of the year as the quarter's loss was absorbed directly into retained earnings, with no dividend distributions in the period.
interim_updates.gaps_note: No QoQ comparison possible: this is the first financial_statements entry for FCT, so there is no prior quarter (e.g. Q4 FY2025/26 ended 31 March 2026) in the database to compare against; yoy_json compares only to the filing's own prior-year comparative quarter (Q1 FY2025/26, ended 30 June 2025). Genuine disclosure gaps: (1) the filing does not break down the Rs.1,170,564k fair-valuation loss by instrument or tenor bucket of the Government Securities book, so the specific bonds/maturities driving the mark-to-market loss cannot be identified; (2) no segmental note is presented (FCT is a single-business primary dealer, so this is expected, not a gap in the ordinary sense); (3) the 100bp May 2026 CBSL policy rate hike and 'Middle East geopolitical tensions' cited as loss drivers in management's Review of Operations (printed page 1) are qualitative commentary only, not quantified by the Company as to their individual contribution to the Rs.1,170,564k fair-valuation loss. Not a gap, but a structural feature documented in this row's notes: FCT's balance sheet is unclassified (no current/non-current split), so current_assets/current_liabilities/inventory/trade_receivables/trade_payables are intentionally blank per this project's bank/NBFI convention, and operating_profit is numerically identical to profit_before_tax because the filing has no intermediate operating-profit subtotal distinct from PBT.
interim_updates.takeaway: FCT's Rs.741.2mn quarterly loss (vs a Rs.1,553.4mn profit a year ago) is a trading-book mark-to-market event, not an erosion of the core repo-funded Government Securities business: a single Rs.1,170.6mn adverse fair-valuation swing more than accounts for the entire profit decline, consistent with management's own attribution to the May 2026 CBSL 100bp rate hike and Middle East-driven market volatility. A Rs.552.1mn one-off recovery of previously-charged management fees/branch commission from parent companies cushioned the loss but should not be read as a repeatable income source next quarter. Leverage continues to build -- the Government Securities book grew to Rs.60.35bn (from Rs.53.60bn at 1 April 2026) funded by a 20.0% quarter-on-quarter rise in repo borrowings to Rs.51.86bn -- worth watching whether the debt/equity ratio (7.95x at 30 June 2026, up from 6.08x at 31 March 2026, per the filing's own investor-information note) and interest cover (0.11x this quarter per the same note) recover once trading conditions normalise.

operational_highlights: Loss After Tax of Rs.741.2mn for Q1 FY2026/27 (quarter ended 30 June 2026) vs Profit After Tax of Rs.1,553.4mn in Q1 FY2025/26 -- a Rs.2,294.6mn swing.
Loss on fair valuation of financial assets through P&L of Rs.1,170.6mn (2025: a Rs.744.6mn gain) -- the single largest driver of the swing, exceeding the entire PAT decline in magnitude.
Net trading income (Direct income less Direct expenses) itself swung to a Rs.297.4mn loss (2025: Rs.1,787.3mn profit) as Direct income fell 74.2% YoY while Direct expenses fell only 30.2%.

Other Income rose to Rs.558.6mn (2025: Rs.6.4mn) almost entirely due to a one-off Rs.552.1mn recovery of management fee (Rs.216.8mn) and branch commission (Rs.238.6mn) plus Rs.96.7mn interest, previously charged by parent companies First Capital Holdings PLC and First Capital Limited.
Operating expenses fell 49.3% YoY to Rs.144.7mn (2025: Rs.285.2mn) on lower admin costs and a 91.3% drop in other operating expenses.

Government Securities trading book grew to Rs.60.35bn at 30 June 2026 from Rs.53.60bn at 1 April 2026, funded by a 20.0% quarter-on-quarter rise in repo borrowings to Rs.51.86bn; total net assets fell to Rs.6.91bn from Rs.7.65bn at the start of the year.
Debt/equity ratio rose to 7.95x at 30 June 2026 from 6.08x at 31 March 2026; interest cover fell to 0.11x for the quarter (both per the filing's own investor-information note).
key_drivers: Rs.1,170.6mn adverse fair-valuation swing on the Government Securities trading book (2025: a Rs.744.6mn gain, a Rs.1,915.2mn negative swing) -- management attributes this to a 100bp CBSL policy rate hike in May 2026 and market volatility linked to Middle East geopolitical tensions; this single line exceeds the entire Rs.2,294.6mn PAT decline.

Direct income (funding-cost-gross trading revenue) fell 74.2% YoY to Rs.906.4mn (2025: Rs.3,513.0mn) while Direct expenses fell only 30.2% to Rs.1,203.8mn (2025: Rs.1,725.8mn) -- funding costs did not scale down proportionately with trading income, turning Net trading income negative.

A one-off Rs.552.1mn recovery of previously-charged management fee and branch commission from parent companies (Note 1.1) cushioned but did not offset the trading-book loss -- flagged as non-recurring.
Net deferred tax asset recognition of Rs.312.8mn (vs a Rs.699.7mn tax expense a year earlier) reduced the pre-tax loss of Rs.1,054.0mn down to a Rs.741.2mn after-tax loss.
